model_annotation: The figure contains two side-by-side time-series line plots illustrating the evolution of an “IWF Fiskalindex” together with a debt ratio (“Schuldenquote”) shown on a secondary y-axis. In both panels, the x-axis is a linear time axis with labeled ticks at 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020, spanning roughly 1995–2020. In the left panel, the left y-axis is labeled “IWF Fiskalindex” and runs from 0 to 2.5 with evenly spaced ticks every 0.5, while the right y-axis is labeled “Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat” and runs from 60 to 120 with ticks every 20. The left panel shows a solid blue line (no markers) for the fiscal index that starts near 0 in 1995, rises to around 0.45 by about 2005, dips to roughly 0.35 around 2007–2008, climbs sharply to about 1.0 around 2010–2012, then declines steadily to near 0.15 by about 2019 before ending around 0.5 in 2020. A solid purple line (no markers) starts near 0.05 in 1995, increases gradually to about 0.45 by around 2005, dips slightly near 2007–2008, then rises strongly from about 0.4–0.5 around 2008–2009 to roughly 1.5 by about 2014–2015, stays near 1.5–1.6 through about 2018, and jumps to about 2.0 around 2019–2020. Two sets of triangle markers represent the debt ratio on the right axis: blue upward triangles form step-like plateaus around ~75 in the late 1990s, ~85 in the mid-2000s, ~95 around 2010, and ~110 from roughly 2012 onward; red upward triangles rise from about ~55 in the mid-1990s to ~60 around 2000, ~80 around 2006–2009, ~90 around 2011–2012, ~100 around 2013–2018, and then sit slightly lower near ~98–100 by 2019–2020. In the right panel, the left y-axis is again labeled “IWF Fiskalindex” and spans from −0.5 to 2.0 with ticks every 0.5, and the right y-axis is labeled “Schuldenquote Zentralstaat” spanning 30 to 70 with ticks every 10. The solid blue fiscal-index line begins slightly below 0 (about −0.1) in 1995, fluctuates around 0 through the late 1990s and early 2000s, reaches about 0.2–0.3 by around 2005, dips near 2007–2008, spikes to about 1.0 around 2010, then trends downward from roughly 0.9 around 2012 to near 0.0 by about 2018, before rising to about 0.6 by 2020. The solid purple line starts around −0.2 in 1995, rises to around 0.2 by about 2004–2005, dips near 2007, then increases sharply to about 1.0 around 2011 and continues upward to roughly 1.3 by about 2015–2017, followed by a jump to about 2.0 around 2019–2020. The right-axis debt markers again appear as step-like triangles: blue upward triangles sit near ~50 through the late 1990s and early 2000s, step to ~55 around 2005–2009, to ~62 around 2010–2012, and to ~70 from about 2013 onward; red upward triangles rise from roughly ~32 in the mid-1990s to ~35 around 1998–2001, to ~40 around 2005–2009, to ~45–50 around 2010–2014, remain near ~50 through about 2017, and then edge down slightly to just under ~50 by 2019–2020.
